[P2] Include JSON-envelope escaping in the truncation budget

Truncation still measures the bare map returned by `render`, but this line serializes that JSON again as a string. For example, input containing 100,000 backslashes occupies roughly 200 KB in the record and 400 KB in the envelope, passing the default 256,000-byte budget while emitting substantially more. This defeats the destination-size safeguard; the overhead is payload-dependent, not just approximately 70 bytes. Include the escaped envelope in truncation's size measurement and test a near-limit, escape-heavy payload against the actual stdout byte count.
